questions.q: A zener diode of zener voltage 30 V is connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. The maximum current through the zener diode is
questions.solution:
Current through Load Resistor $\left(I_L\right)$ Since the zener diode regulates the voltage at 30 V , the voltage across the load resistor ( $R_L=6 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ ) will also be 30 V .
The current through the load resistor, $I_L$, is: $I_L=\frac{V_Z}{R_L}=\frac{30 \mathrm{~V}}{6 \mathrm{k} \Omega}=5 \mathrm{~mA}$ Total Current in the Circuit ( $I_{\text{total }}$ ) The total current supplied by the source, $I_{\text{total, }}$, is given by: $I_{\text{total }}=\frac{V_{\text{in }}-V_Z}{R_{\text{total }}}$ where $R_{\text{total }}=5 k \Omega+2 k \Omega=7 k \Omega$. For maximum $I_{\text{total, }}$, we use the maximum input voltage $V_{\text{in }}=100 \mathrm{~V}$ : $I_{\text{total }}=\frac{100 \mathrm{~V}-30 \mathrm{~V}}{7 k \Omega}=\frac{70 \mathrm{~V}}{7 \mathrm{k} \Omega}=10 \mathrm{~mA}$ Maximum Zener Diode Current ( $I_{Z \max }$ ) The zener diode current $I_Z$ is the difference between the total current and the load current: $I_{Z \max }=I_{\text{total }}-I_L=10 m A-5 m A=5 m A$ Final Answer The maximum current through the zener diode is: $5 m A$

What is the binding energy of $S 1429 i$ whose atomic mass is $28. 976495u$

Mass of proton $= 1. 007276u$

Mass of neutron $= 1. 008664u$

(Neglect the electron mass) (Assume $1u = 931. 5MeV$)
questions.solution:
Given: Atomic mass of $S 1429 i$ is $28. 976495u$.

Mass of proton $= 1. 007276u$

Mass of neutron $= 1. 008664u$

The binding energy for $S 1429 i$ can& be calculated& from the mass defect.

$B. E = ∆ mc^{2}$, where $∆ m$ is the change in mass and $c$ is the speed of light.

In $S 1429 i$ number of neutrons are $29 - 14 = 15$ and the number of protons is $14$.

Hence, change in mass is

Thus, the binding energy is

$B. E = 0. 255359 \times 931. 5MeV = 237. 86MeV$

questions.solution: Using KVL to CE circuit, $\begin{array}{rlrl} V_{C C} & =i_C R_C+V_{C E}+i_E R_E & \\ & =i_C R_C+V_{C E}+i_C R_E & \left(\because i_E \approx i_C\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad V_{C E} & =V_{C C}-i_C\left( R_C+R_E\right) & & \ldots(\mathrm{i}) \end{array}$ By Ohm's law, current $i_1$ is; i_1=$\frac{V_{C C}}{R_1+R_2}=\frac{10 \mathrm{ V}}{15 \mathrm{k} \Omega}=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{ mA}$ Now, $\begin{aligned} V_2 & =i_1 R_2 \\ & =\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{ mA} \times5 \mathrm{k} \Omega=\frac{10}{3}\\ V_2 & =3.3 \mathrm{ V} \end{aligned}$ KVL to base circuit gives, $V_2=V_{B E}+i_E R_E$ For silicon transistor, $\begin{aligned} V_{B E} & =0.7 \mathrm{ V} \Rightarrow i_E=\frac{V_2-V_{B E}}{R_E}\\ & =\frac{3.3-0.7}{526} \approx5 \mathrm{ mA} \end{aligned}$ So, $\quad i_C \approx i_E=5 \mathrm{ mA}$ Hence, from $\mathrm{Eq}$ (i) $V_{C E}$ is $\begin{aligned} V_{C E} & =V_{C C}-i_C\left( R_C+R_E\right) \\ & =10-5 \mathrm{ mA}(1 \mathrm{k} \Omega+526 \Omega) \\ & \approx2.4 \mathrm{ V} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a transistor circuit, when the base current is increased by 50 micro-amperes keeping the collector voltage fixed at 2 volts, the collector current increases by $1 \mathrm{ mA}$. The current gain of the transistor is
questions.solution:
Increase in base current $\Delta$ I_b=50 \mu $\mathrm{A}$ Increase in collector current $\Delta I_c=1 \mathrm{ mA}$
Current gain $\beta=\frac{\Delta I_c}{\Delta I_b}=\frac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{50 \times 10^{-6}}=\frac{10^3}{50}=20$

questions.q: While a collector to emitter voltage is constant in a transistor, the collector current changes by 8.2 mA when the emitter current changes by $8.3 \mathrm{ mA}$. The value of forward current ratio is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta I_c=8.2 \mathrm{ mA} \\ & \qquad \Delta I_c=8.3 \mathrm{ mA} \\ & \text{ Base current } \Delta I_b=\Delta I_c-\Delta I_c=8.3-8.2=0.1 \mathrm{ mA} \\ & \therefore \text{ Forward current ratio }=\frac{\Delta I_c}{\Delta I_b}=\frac{8.2}{0.1}=82\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a Zener regulated power supply a Zener diode with $V_z=6 \mathrm{ V}$ is used for regulation. The load current is $4 \mathrm{ mA}$ and the unregulated input voltage is $10 \mathrm{ V}$. To get a Zener current five times the load current the value of series resistor $R_S$ is nearly
questions.solution:
Given, $I_Z=5 I_L=20 \mathrm{ mA}$
Total current $I_s$ through $R_s$ is $I_s=I_Z+I_L=20+4=24 \mathrm{ mA}$ As a potential drop of $6 \mathrm{ V}$ occurs across Zener diode and supply voltage is $10 \mathrm{ V}$. So, potential drop across $R_s, V_s=10-6=4 \mathrm{ V}\therefore$ Series resistor, $R_s=\frac{V_s}{I_s}=\frac{4}{24 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 167 \Omega$
